managed.title: Managed backups — Neon PITR
managed.body: Database backups are managed by Neon via continuous point-in-time recovery (PITR) — documented {days}-day retention window. There is no app-owned snapshot job, so no "last backup" time is shown here — restore is branch-from-history by timestamp (see runbook).

posture.disclaimer: Values are documented (target/configured), not a live system read. Verify the actual retention window in the Neon console per the runbook.

piiKey.title: Critical dependency — PII encryption keys
piiKey.warning: A database restore alone is not enough.
piiKey.body: PII is encrypted with pgcrypto using PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY / PII_HASH_KEY held in Infisical — NOT in the database. Without recovering the matching keys, a restored database is unreadable ciphertext. The keys must be recoverable (Infisical + an offline escrow).

drill.title: Restore drill — proven, not assumed
drill.body: An untested restore is as dangerous as no backup. A periodic restore drill (at least quarterly) is run, including an end-to-end PII decryption check. If PII does not decrypt, the drill fails. See the drill checklist in the runbook.

runbook.title: Operator runbook
runbook.body: The full step-by-step restore procedure (Neon branch-restore, pg_dump/pg_restore fallback, key recovery, R2 backup) is documented in:
